planReference.rule: All dependencies verified plus group legacy-save, undo, reopen, complete-backup/restore and actual UI/client tests; separate reviewed activation receipt.

change: CREATIVE_DOCUMENTS_ENABLED = true (core/documents.ts). The YAMAKAN_AG_DOCS_QUALIFICATION test switch is removed; YAMAKAN_AG_DOCS_OFF=1 in the service's own environment is the operator rollback.

members.state: VERIFIED (part a; part b with YU-014)

covers: real service started as a user starts it (no switch), capability available
SDK: Studio bitmap upload and a canvas naming it; MCP yamakan_document_save of a Cinema scene; CLI stage-document committed with its printed receipt
legacy whole-project save (yamakan.project.save) keeps every document
typed batch, undo and redo through commands: the scene is removed and restored, documents unchanged
legacy Cinema sidecar inventory and migration into the project, original kept
hard kill (SIGKILL) and reopen on the same workspace: identical document bytes and bitmap
backup and restore through commands (creative: complete), a second service on the restored workspace reads identical documents, bitmap and the legacy file
rollback: a service with YAMAKAN_AG_DOCS_OFF=1 reports turnedOff, reads every document and the bitmap, and refuses saves and bitmap uploads with the operator reason
installed Edge over CDP: create, draw, save, conflicting save, reload
service killed between phases; reopen shows the saved canvas
backup and restore through the SDK; a service on the restored workspace reopens the same canvas in Edge
each workspace checked independently of the browser (v5 head, one Studio document, stored bitmaps matching their digests)

refusalPathsUnderRollback: tests/document-clients.test.ts (SDK, MCP, CLI against the real service)

hardeningWithActivation: Agents cannot migrate legacy scenes (a source belongs to the first project it enters)
Agents share one 8 MiB staging pool of their own; with the browser's and the local client's own shares the workspace holds 24 MiB, so agents can never lock out either
Workspace-wide budgets: Studio bitmaps 8 GiB, distinct stored document bytes 4 GiB; agents write only while the workspace uses less than half of each, so the person always keeps the rest
Garbage collection runs hourly (unreferenced bitmaps and refused uploads' files are freed while the service runs)
Stored documents and bitmaps stay readable through the API under rollback; Studio becomes session-only and says saved canvases are kept and return when saving is turned back on
An unrecognised YAMAKAN_AG_DOCS_OFF value is announced at startup

rollbackProcedure: Set YAMAKAN_AG_DOCS_OFF=1 in the service's environment and restart: every write path refuses, stored documents and bitmaps stay readable and keep their references. A code rollback sets CREATIVE_DOCUMENTS_ENABLED back to false; v5 projects stay readable either way.
limitations: The Cinema viewport still saves workspace sidecars (yamakan.scene.save); they are backed up (YU-014) and migratable (YU-012). Moving Cinema UI saves into project documents is follow-up work (YU-030 project selection).
The browser's legacy whole-project save is exercised through the same yamakan.project.save command by the SDK, not from the editor UI after a canvas save
Workspace budgets are not exercised at their limits by a test; stored document versions are never pruned, so the 4 GiB document budget is a lifetime cap until revision pruning exists
Agent limits apply to agent tokens; an MCP server started without an agent token acts as the local client
Studio under rollback is checked by code review, not by a browser test
Browser tabs share one undo writer (YU-015 limitation)
Full OCR review blocked (cloud provider configured; local model needs more free RAM)
